import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 828

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/828](https://www.erdosproblems.com/828)
-/

namespace Erdos828

open scoped Nat

/--
Is it true that, for any $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$$\phi(n) | n + a$$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_828 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ a : ℤ, Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | ↑(φ n) ∣ n + a} := by
  sorry

/--
When $n > 1$, Lehmer conjectured that $\phi(n) | n - 1$ if and only if $n$ is prime.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_828.variants.lehmer_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n > 1, φ n ∣ n - 1 ↔ Prime n := by
  sorry

/--
It is an easy exercise to show that $\phi(n) | n$ if and only if $n = 0, 1$ or $n = 2^a 3^b$ for
some $a > 0$.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/XC0R/formal-conjectures/blob/03e00cf8d44098d0fb06e891fca30c29769df619/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/828.lean#L49"]
theorem erdos_828.variants.phi_dvd_self_iff_pow2_pow3 {n : ℕ} :
    φ n ∣ n ↔ n ≤ 1 ∨ ∃ᵉ (a > 0) (b), n = 2 ^ a * 3 ^ b := by
  sorry

end Erdos828

reformulations.difference: The solution set ranges over all natural numbers, including zero, rather than restricting Euler's totient to positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed integer a, imposing n > 0 removes at most the single element 0, so infinitude is unchanged. In Mathlib φ(0)=0, and zero belongs to the original solution set exactly when a=0. The equivalence, including the outer quantifier over a, was proved independently in Review828.main_positive_iff.

review.notes:
No Lean mathematical defect was identified in the three declarations. The cited website still labels the main problem open, and Wikipedia records Lehmer's problem as unsolved.

There is a source-side typo worth clarifying: the website's current LaTeX says φ(n) ∣ n iff n=2^a3^b for a,b≥0. This incorrectly includes n=3, since φ(3)=2 does not divide 3. Lean correctly requires a>0 and separately includes 0 and 1. This is a correction of the elementary remark, not an equivalence to its erroneous literal wording; the Lean statement should not be weakened to match that typo.

/workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully. It checks the elaborated types and boundary cases, tests both variants through n=500, proves the harmless boundary extensions and the Lehmer formulation's equivalence to having no composite solution, and verifies the source-side n=3 counterexample. These proofs do not depend on sorryAx. The reviewed file was not modified.
